title: Developing A Context-Aware English-Ebira Translation System Using Fine-Tuned T5 Transformer and Position-Aware Idiom Detection
abstract: Ebira is a language spoken by the Ebira people, known as "Anebira," a minority ethnic group spreading across five states and predominantly located in Kogi Central, Nigeria. The Ebira-speaking community of approximately 2.5 million faces a compounding linguistic crisis where about 35% of the older generation, though fluent in Ebira, remains largely excluded from the socioeconomic and knowledge advantages mediated through English, while younger generations are progressively abandoning their mother tongue in pursuit of English-driven social mobility, educational achievement, and economic inclusion, placing the language at risk of functional extinction without guaranteeing full English proficiency in return. Machine Translation (MT) had been adopted as a viable solution; however, the two existing English-Ebira rule-based systems suffer from poor fluency, limited accuracy, inability to translate idiomatic phrases, and significant loss of linguistic nuance. While NMT systems developed for related low-resource languages such as Nigerian Pidgin, and Igala show promising result with improvement in fluency and general translation accuracy, critical structural limitations persist: their models cannot distinguish literal from idiomatic content within the same sentence, fail on paraphrased idiomatic expressions, and produce translations that are structurally fluent but culturally hollow. To address these challenges, this research developed a unidirectional English-Ebira translation system built around a fine-tuned T5-base transformer model for general sentence translation with improved fluency, accuracy and proper handling of the nuances, incorporating a position-aware idiom detection layer for differential translation of mixed literal-idiomatic sentences, and a Sentence-BERT (SBERT) semantic embedding model with dictionary-enhanced detection for culturally validated idiomatic translation. The system was trained on 32,322 English–Ebira parallel sentence pairs, the T5-base model achieved a BLEU score of 40.95% with a 100% translation success rate. The hybrid system substantially outperformed both a rule-based baseline and the T5-only model on idiomatic content: on a 200-sentence idiomatic evaluation set, the T5-only model reached 8.5% of sentences at or above the 0.5 BLEU threshold, while the hybrid system achieved 90%, representing a relative gain of approximately 959%. On general translation, the hybrid system similarly outperformed the rule-based baseline, achieving 87% of test sentences at or above the 0.5 BLEU threshold compared to 81.5% for the baseline (McNemar chi-square = 6.37, p = 0.012). Human evaluation produced a mean cultural relevance score of 8.4/10, supporting hybrid symbolic-neural architectures for culturally appropriate low-resource translation.

evidence.title: Developing A Context-Aware English-Ebira Translation System Using Fine-Tuned T5 Transformer and Position-Aware Idiom Detection
evidence.abstract: Ebira is a language spoken by the Ebira people, known as "Anebira," a minority ethnic group spreading across five states and predominantly located in Kogi Central, Nigeria. The Ebira-speaking community of approximately 2.5 million faces a compounding linguistic crisis where about 35% of the older generation, though fluent in Ebira, remains largely excluded from the socioeconomic and knowledge advantages mediated through English, while younger generations are progressively abandoning their mother tongue in pursuit of English-driven social mobility, educational achievement, and economic inclusion, placing the language at risk of functional extinction without guaranteeing full English proficiency in return. Machine Translation (MT) had been adopted as a viable solution; however, the two existing English-Ebira rule-based systems suffer from poor fluency, limited accuracy, inability to translate idiomatic phrases, and significant loss of linguistic nuance. While NMT systems developed for related low-resource languages such as Nigerian Pidgin, and Igala show promising result with improvement in fluency and general translation accuracy, critical structural limitations persist: their models cannot distinguish literal from idiomatic content within the same sentence, fail on paraphrased idiomatic expressions, and produce translations that are structurally fluent but culturally hollow. To address these challenges, this research developed a unidirectional English-Ebira translation system built around a fine-tuned T5-base transformer model for general sentence translation with improved fluency, accuracy and proper handling of the nuances, incorporating a position-aware idiom detection layer for differential translation of mixed literal-idiomatic sentences, and a Sentence-BERT (SBERT) semantic embedding model with dictionary-enhanced detection for culturally validated idiomatic translation. The system was trained on 32,322 English–Ebira parallel sentence pairs, the T5-base model achieved a BLEU score of 40.95% with a 100% translation success rate. The hybrid system substantially outperformed both a rule-based baseline and the T5-only model on idiomatic content: on a 200-sentence idiomatic evaluation set, the T5-only model reached 8.5% of sentences at or above the 0.5 BLEU threshold, while the hybrid system achieved 90%, representing a relative gain of approximately 959%. On general translation, the hybrid system similarly outperformed the rule-based baseline, achieving 87% of test sentences at or above the 0.5 BLEU threshold compared to 81.5% for the baseline (McNemar chi-square = 6.37, p = 0.012). Human evaluation produced a mean cultural relevance score of 8.4/10, supporting hybrid symbolic-neural architectures for culturally appropriate low-resource translation.

title: Disseny i desenrotllament d'un sistema basat en intel·ligència artificial per a la classificació automàtica de biòpsies de càncer de pròstata segons l'escala de Gleason
abstract: [EN] El càncer de pròstata constituïx actualment la neoplàsia més diagnosticada en hòmens a nivell mundial i una de les principals causes de mortalitat per càncer a Europa i els Estats Units. El diagnòstic es fonamenta principalment en la biòpsia prostàtica, que permet l’avaluació histopatològica del teixit i l’assignació d’un valor en l’escala escala de Gleason que reflectix l’agressivitat del càncer. El valor d’escala de Gleason s’obté a partir de la suma dels graus Gleason primari i segundario de la biòpsia. Cada un d’estos patrons Gleason es definix per unes característiques morfològiques de les cèl·lules, diferenciant-se en cinc nivells. L’escala de Gleason obtinguda orienta el pronòstic i guia la decisió de tractament adequat per a cada pacient. La digitalització de les imatges histològiques en forma de Whole Slide Images (WSI) ha permés el seu emmagatzematge digital i el seu ús per a l’aplicació de tècniques d’intel·ligència artificial (IA). No obstant això, un dels principals reptes de les WSI és la seua gran grandària si es volen emprar en l’entrenament de models d’IA, per això, s’empra la tècnica d’apedaçament, dividint cada imatge en pegats o imatges de menor grandària que poden ser usats en l’entrenament de models. Els pegats permeten conserven els detalls discriminatius de les WSI, representant estos detalls en l’extracció de característiques. Les característiques s’extrauen mitjançant models que identifiquen patrons rellevants en les dades. S’avaluaran models fundacionals, és a dir, models preentrenados amb gran conjunts de dades en la seua forma original i després de fine-turning per a la tasca concreta, així com extractors propis. Els models fundacionals permeten extraure característiques, aprofitant la seua capacitat per a transferir coneixement des de dominis generals a l’àmbit biomèdic. L’objectiu d’este TFM consistix en el desenrotllament d’un algorisme de predicció basat en tècniques d’aprenentatge profund per a la classificació de biòpsies segons l’escala de Gleason. En concret, s’avaluaran diferents metodologies d’extracció de característiques sobre els pegats, incloent-hi la implementació de mètodes basats en grafs per a la classificació de les biòpsies segons l’Escala Gleason. L’enfocament en grafs aprofita la naturalesa del problema, la relació dels pegats de cada WSI entre si per a modeles les relacions i capturar patrons de similitud i estructures entre els pegats. Sobre estes representacions s’apliquen xarxes neuronals de grafs (GNN). Per a entrenar l’arquitectura proposada, s’empraran bases de dades públiques d’imatges histològiques completes (WSI) que contenen anotacions del grau Gleason primari i secundari corresponents a cada biòpsia. Finalment, és important destacar que el sistema també incorporarà mecanismes de explicabilidad que permeten identificar, dins de les imatges histològiques completes (WSI), les regions més rellevants associades als graus Gleason primari i secundari.

title: Hybrid Capsule Network with Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Feature Extraction and Tumor Localization in Lung Cancer Detection from CT Scans
abstract: The model was evaluated on the LIDC-IDRI lung CT dataset using standard performance measures, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC). The experimental findings show that the proposed framework attains 83.33% accuracy, 85.00% precision, 80.95% recall, 82.93% F1-score, MCC of 0.6674, and AUC of 0.9045, outperforming baseline classifiers including Decision Tree, Voting Classifier, AdaBoost, and Stacking. Early detection of lung cancer is crucial for patient survival, but conventional Neural Networks (CNNs) often fail to detect and localize tumors due to their limited spatial and relational knowledge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid Capsule Network-Graph Neural Network (CapsNet-GNN) architecture. The Caps Net module extracts hierarchical and spatial information from CT scans of the lung, whereas the GNN module simulates inter-nodule relationships to improve tumor localization. The contributions of the Caps Net and GNN modules are also confirmed in ablation studies, which show that Caps Net and GNN complement each other in feature representation and relational learning. These findings provide statistical support for the soundness, generality, and clinical usefulness of the suggested framework, offer a dependable answer to automated lung cancer identification and tumor localization, and can be incorporated into clinical decision-support mechanisms.

title: Artifact for Datura: Progressive Red Teaming Testing for Tool Invocation Chain in LLM Agents
abstract: Artifact for the paper "Datura: Progressive Red Teaming Testing for Tool Invocation Chain in LLM Agents." This artifact is prepared for the ISSTA 2026 Artifact Evaluation and requests the Reusable and Available badges. It includes source code, benchmark inputs, defense implementations, metric prompts, Datura main-run raw outputs, and scripts for evaluation with an API key. Artifact contents:- datura-issta2026-artifact.tar.gz: source package, README, scripts, benchmark inputs, defenses, and results.zip- datura-ae-docker-image.tar: prebuilt Docker image for the containerized review path- CHECKSUMS.txt: SHA-256 checksums for the two archives The included results.zip contains Datura main-run raw outputs for 5 models under no_defense / prompt_refuge / dify_defense / khoj_defense. To unpack the source package: mkdir datura-issta2026-artifacttar -xzf datura-issta2026-artifact.tar.gz -C datura-issta2026-artifactcd datura-issta2026-artifact Containerized package check: docker load -i ../datura-ae-docker-image.tardocker run --rm datura-ae Expected final line: Package check passed. No API key was required. Native Python package check: python3 -m venv .venv. .venv/bin/activatepip install -r requirements-ae.txtpython scripts/package_check.py The package check verifies that required files are present, 740 benign tasks load, the pipeline initializes, results.zip is readable, and no API key is bundled in the artifact. API configuration: The artifact does not include API credentials. To run experiments, provide an OpenAI-compatible key through environment variables: export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key"export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://api.openai.com/v1" The default endpoint is the official OpenAI API endpoint. Change OPENAI_BASE_URL only when intentionally using another OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Small API evaluation: python run_full_evaluation.py \ --target_model gpt-4.1 \ --defense no_defense \ --start_idx 0 \ --end_idx 5 \ --max_workers 1 The output is written under results/ as: results/datura_gpt-4_1_no_defense.json Metric evaluation for a generated result file: python evaluate_metrics.py results/datura_gpt-4_1_no_defense.json \ --metrics ph asr rr \ --max_workers 1 Inspect the included raw outputs without calling an API: python scripts/inspect_results.py results.zip Supported defense identifiers:- no_defense- prompt_refuge- khoj_defense- dify_defense Complete API evaluation for one model/defense setting: python run_full_evaluation.py \ --target_model gpt-4.1 \ --defense no_defense \ --start_idx 0 \ --end_idx 740 \ --max_workers 40 This run may take substantial time and incur API cost. The artifact supports the paper claims about chained tool hijacking attacks, the three-stage Datura pipeline, comparisons across target models and defense mechanisms, and metrics for prompt harmlessness, goal progress, and agent helpfulness.

title: A Context-Aware Text Sentiment Classification Framework Leveraging Pretrained Large Language Models and Transfer Learning for Large-Scale Opinion Mining
abstract: The proliferation of user-generated digital text across social media platforms, e-commerce ecosystems, and online discourse forums has established large-scale opinion mining as a critical capability for organisations seeking actionable intelligence from unstructured data. Classical lexicon-driven and shallow machine learning approaches to sentiment classification are demonstrably insufficient for capturing the compositional, context-dependent, and often irony-laden polarity signals embedded in contemporary natural language. The advent of self-supervised pretrained transformer architectures—most notably the BERT family and its successors—has redefined the performance ceiling for sentiment analysis; however, significant gaps persist in exploiting contextual disambiguation at the document level, adapting general-purpose language representations to domain-specific opinion vocabularies, and preserving classification performance under low-resource conditions. Despite impressive benchmark scores, existing transfer-learning frameworks for sentiment classification encounter four persistent limitations: (i) shallow context integration that fails to model long-range sentiment dependencies spanning multiple clauses; (ii) domain mismatch between pretraining corpora and target-domain lexicons resulting in systematic misclassification of domain-specific sentiment expressions; (iii) poor calibration under distributional shift, manifesting as overconfident incorrect predictions on adversarial and out-of-domain inputs; and (iv) prohibitive computational cost of full fine-tuning for large-scale transformer models in resource-constrained deployment environments. This dissertation introduces the Context-Aware Transfer Language Model (CAT-LLM) framework, integrating DeBERTa-v3-Large as the contextual encoder with three complementary components: a Context-Aware Position Encoding (CAPE) module that augments disentangled attention with document-level positional signals; a parameter-efficient Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning strategy with layer-wise learning-rate decay; and a Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty estimation head providing calibrated confidence scores alongside sentiment predictions. Evaluated across six benchmark datasets—SST-2, IMDb, Yelp-5, Amazon Reviews, Twitter SemEval, and SemEval 2017—the CAT-LLM framework achieved macro F1-scores of 0.962, 0.958, 0.924, 0.941, 0.887, and 0.903 respectively, surpassing all baselines including RoBERTa-Large and XLNet-Large by margins of 1.5–7.5%. AUC-ROC reached 0.984. With only 10 training examples, CAT-LLM achieved 71.2% accuracy—12.7 percentage points above BiLSTM—demonstrating exceptional few-shot transferability. The CAT-LLM framework establishes a new state of the art for large-scale opinion mining, reconciling contextual expressiveness, parameter efficiency, and uncertainty quantification within a unified, production-deployable sentiment analysis pipeline.

title: EMBRACING INNOVATION: DIGITAL TOOLS SHAPING THE FUTURE OF HOTEL OPERATIONS
authors: Prof. Shrikala Sawant & Dr. Megha Bhargava
abstract: The incorporation of digital tools to optimise hotel operations is causing a revolutionary change in the hospitality sector. This study investigates how operational performance, customer happiness, and cost-effectiveness in hotel management are affected by developing technologies including artificial intelligence, cloud-based property management systems, and mobile applications. Using a mixed-methods approach, the study combines qualitative information from semi-structured interviews with other industry professionals with quantitative data collected from structured surveys of hotel managers in Mumbai area. In order to guarantee a varied representation of hotel sizes and service categories, the data gathering was carried out. Results point to a strong relationship between the use of digital tools and enhancements in areas including food ordering, guest experience, data-driven decision-making, and visitor check-in/check-out procedures. Obstacles were also noted, such as initial implementation expenses and personnel challenge. In order to exploit the advantages of digital transformation, this article emphasizes the need for strategic planning and employee training. The findings give a thorough grasp of how technology is changing hotel operations and have useful ramifications for industry participants hoping to maintain their competitiveness in a quickly changing environment

title: Intermediate-Task Training for Cross-Lingual Robustness in XTREME Subsets
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does intermediate-task training improve robustness to typological divergence in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XTREME subsets compared to direct fine-tuning? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: EpiSwarm: reproducibility package (code, data, and statistical analysis)
abstract: Reproducibility package for the article "Epigenetic regulation for dynamic UAV-swarm optimization—EpiSwarm" (Computing and Artificial Intelligence, 2026, 4(1), 4448; DOI: 10.59400/cai4448). Contains the simulation code (EpiSwarm plus four baselines: greedy, static GA, adaptive GA, and memory-archive GA), the matched n=20 ablation runner, raw batch results (5,580 rows) and matched-ablation data (540 rows) in CSV and pandas-pickle form, the computed Wilcoxon signed-rank statistics, and self-contained notebooks that reproduce the tables and figures. Parameter grids and scenario seeds are documented in the README. Requires Python 3.10+ with numpy, pandas, and scipy. Released under the MIT License.

title: AgentBreaker: Evaluating Context-Aware Indirect Prompt Injection Risks in Modern Web Agents (Artifact)
abstract: LLM-powered web agents are already deployed at consumer scale. Despite their increasing use for web automation, their security implications under Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attacks remain largely understudied, while existing attack methods achieve relatively low attack success rates (ASRs). AgentBreaker is an automated framework for generating context-aware indirect prompt injection attacks by composing adversarial phrases tailored to the HTML context of each target webpage. This artifact consists of the following components:A. Target HTML pages collected from Online-Mind2WebB. AgentBreaker source codeC. Docker images for the target web agentsD. Docker images and scripts for reproducing the experiments presented in the paperE. Sample results for attacks

This artifact consists of the following components:A. Target HTML pages collected from Online-Mind2WebB. AgentBreaker source codeC. Docker images for the target web agentsD. Docker images and scripts for reproducing the experiments presented in the paperE. Sample results for attacks

title: Optimized Skill Mastery Prediction for Adaptive Test Decision-Making
abstract: Adaptive testing systems require accurate and timely estimation of students' skill mastery levels to support decision-making in question selection and assessment flow determination. However, uncertainty in students' knowledge levels and variations in learning behavior often limit the performance of conventional predictive models. This study proposes an optimized predictive modeling framework for skill mastery to enhance decision-making quality in adaptive testing. The proposed framework integrates a machine learning-based skill mastery prediction model with an optimization mechanism to improve model accuracy and stability, while accommodating the sequential nature and uncertainty of student responses. Learning interaction data is used to dynamically model the development of skill mastery levels, which are then utilized as decision-support input in the adaptive testing system. The proposed predictive skill mastery model shows strong and consistent performance with an AUC value of 0.822, Average Precision of 0.868, accuracy of 0.757, and a precision balance of 0.834, recall of 0.788, and F1-score of 0.810, supported by well-calibrated probabilities and the ability to respond adaptively to student learning dynamics, making it suitable for use to support decision-making in adaptive test decision-making systems. The results of this study confirm the potential of integrating predictive analytics and optimization techniques in developing intelligent adaptive assessment systems.

title: ОНТОЛОГІЧНА МОДЕЛЬ ПРЕДМЕТНОЇ ОБЛАСТІ «ІНТЕЛЕКТУАЛЬНИЙ АСИСТЕНТ ВИКЛАДАЧА ІТ-ГАЛУЗІ»
abstract: У статті досліджено проблему формалізованого подання знань у предметній області інтелектуального асистента викладача ІТ-галузі з урахуванням специфіки сучасних освітніх технологій і динамічного розвитку інформаційних технологій. Обґрунтовано доцільність застосування онтологічного підходу як засобу структуризації знань, забезпечення їх узгодженості та можливості інтеграції з інтелектуальними системами. На основі системного аналізу професійної діяльності викладача та структури освітнього процесу визначено ключові групи концептів предметної області, які охоплюють суб’єктів навчання, структурні компоненти освітнього процесу, навчальну діяльність, доменні об’єкти ІТ-галузі, функціональні можливості інтелектуального асистента та освітні дані. Запропоновано онтологічну модель, що забезпечує інтеграцію педагогічної та технічної складових у межах єдиної формалізованої структури. Особливістю моделі є врахування специфіки ІТ-освіти, зокрема формалізованого характеру результатів навчання у вигляді програмного коду, а також необхідності його аналізу, тестування та оцінювання. Розроблена модель включає систему семантичних зв’язків між концептами, що дозволяє відобразити як структуру освітнього процесу, так і процеси програмної діяльності. Додатково запропоновано формалізоване подання інтелектуального асистента як системи опрацювання даних і знань, що забезпечує генерацію навчального контенту, аналітику освітньої діяльності та формування рекомендацій. Обґрунтовано доцільність інтеграції онтологічних моделей із сучасними технологіями штучного інтелекту, зокрема великими мовними моделями, що дозволяє підвищити точність, інтерпретованість та адаптивність інтелектуальних освітніх систем. Отримані результати мають теоретичне значення для розвитку методів подання знань у освітніх системах та практичну цінність для розроблення інтелектуальних асистентів викладача в ІТ-освіті.

title: Analisis Sentimen Terhadap Kinerja Menteri Keuangan Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa Menggunakan Algoritma K-Nearest Neighbors
abstract: Perkembangan media sosial meningkatkan partisipasi publik dalam menyampaikan opini terhadap kebijakan dan kinerja pejabat pemerintah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis sentimen terhadap kinerja Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa sebagai Menteri Keuangan berdasarkan komentar TikTok. Data diperoleh melalui teknik scraping dari video TikTok dalam periode satu bulan setelah pelantikan dan menghasilkan 1317 komentar setelah proses pembersihan data. Tahapan pengolahan meliputi preprocessing, pelabelan data menggunakan metode manual dan lexicon-based, ekstraksi fitur menggunakan TF-IDF serta pemodelan menggunakan algoritma K-Nearest Neighbors. Penentuan parameter optimal dilakukan menggunakan GridSearchCV dengan 10-Fold Cross Validation, yang menghasilkan nilai K terbaik 13 untuk data dengan labeling manual dan 15 untuk data dengan labeling lexicon-based. Hasil pengujian menggunakan Holdout Validation (80:20) menunjukkan bahwa model KNN dengan labeling manual memperoleh akurasi tertinggi sebesar 94,32%, sedangkan model dengan lexicon-based memperoleh akurasi sebesar 75,38%. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pelabelan manual menghasilkan performa klasifikasi yang lebih baik dan lebih konsisten dibandingkan metode lexicon-based. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa kualitas pelabelan data berpengaruh signifikan terhadap performa klasifikasi sentimen, terutama pada komentar media sosial yang bersifat informal dan ambigu.

title: Smart Ecosystem Performance Optimization Using Federated Learning For Iot-Based Real-Time Data Processing
abstract: The rapid expansion of smart ecosystems driven by Internet of Things (IoT) technologies requires real-time data processing that is secure, efficient, and capable of handling large-scale heterogeneous data streams. Traditional centralized learning approaches often struggle with latency, bandwidth constraints, and privacy risks due to the continuous transfer of raw data. This study aims to optimize smart ecosystem performance by integrating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed intelligence framework for real-time IoT data processing. The proposed model allows multiple IoT nodes to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, thereby enhancing privacy protection and reducing network load. Experimental results demonstrate that FL provides higher accuracy, better scalability, and improved resilience compared to centralized systems, especially in environments with diverse sensor distributions. These findings confirm that Federated Learning is a highly promising approach for strengthening smart ecosystem reliability, responsiveness, and data security. This research contributes to developing future-ready IoT architectures capable of supporting intelligent, decentralized, and privacy-preserving environments

title: Reducing the TCB of SGX-Oriented LibOSes at Runtime
abstract: Intel Software Guard Extensions (SGX) provides a trusted execution environment (TEE) for applications to protect runtime code and data from the untrusted environment. All code residing in the enclave, including LibOSes and the libraries, is all taken into the Trusted Computing Base (TCB). The TCB size closely correlates with the potential vulnerabilities and the system’s attack surface. Vulnerabilities in the enclave can tamper with the control flow of the enclave program and potentially lead to data breaches. Existing SGX frameworks present a dilemma: either include a large LibOS in the enclave to ensure functionality, which inflates the TCB and attack surface, or move the OS out for a minimal TCB, which severely restricts application support or incurs high overhead, insecure interactions with the untrusted world. In this paper, we introduce DynaTCB, a runtime framework designed to balance security and functionality. To enhance security, DynaTCB dynamically adjusts the TCB according to runtime program behavior. To preserve functionality, it logically removes unneeded code from the TCB instead of physically removing it from the enclave, thus avoiding the drawbacks of frequent untrusted interactions. It performs binary-level analysis without requiring source code. Experimental results show that DynaTCB achieves a code reduction of over 95% for the Coreutils suite and more than 80% for real-world applications with 14.2% overhead. Additionally, DynaTCB successfully breaks the gadget chains in SGX and mitigates several Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs), affirming its potential to significantly enhance security in SGX environments.

title: Multilingual Evaluation of Semantic Robustness and Cultural Adaptability in Transformer Models for Emotion Recognition
abstract: Multilingual language models achieve strong results in emotion classification; however, their robustness under culturally complex and linguistically diverse conditions remains limited. Standard evaluations rely on structured datasets that do not capture phenomena such as code-switching, idiomatic expressions, and indirect affective language, which are common in real-world communication. This study introduces a culturally oriented evaluation framework to analyze the behavior of mBERT, XLM-R, and a fine-tuned variant (XLM-R-FT) under non-standard linguistic conditions. The evaluation combines a multilingual dataset with a subset of manually annotated samples incorporating regional variation in Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian. Results show consistent performance degradation on culturally marked inputs, with reductions of up to 10 F1 points. Fine-tuning improves stability but does not eliminate sensitivity to implicit and idiomatic expressions. Interpretability analysis using LIME and SHAP indicates that predictions are often driven by lexically salient tokens, leading to misinterpretations. The proposed framework enables evaluation beyond standard benchmarks and highlights the need to incorporate cultural and linguistic variability in multilingual emotion analysis.

title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
abstract: To improve safety in Large Language Models (LLMs) we can either perform post-training alignment or exploit refusal directions in the activation space. Both strategies are less feasible in Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) as they require unsafe multimodal data, harder to collect than their unimodal counterpart. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a light-weight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation re-centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak benchmarks, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility. These results reveal that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.

title: BARTZ V. ANTHROPIC: FAIR USE IN BALANCING AI TECHNOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT AND COPYRIGHT IN AI TRAINING DATA
abstract: Access to copyright works is central to the training of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models, particularly, Large Language Models (LLMs). This paper reviews the application of the doctrine of fair use to AI training data by the US Court in Bartz et al. v. Anthropic in comparison to the earlier case of Thomson Reuters Enter. Centre GmbH v. Ross Intell. Inc and latter decision in Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc. The paper argues that Bartz v. Anthropic may provide some guidance in balancing the interests of AI development and copyright owners by separating the issues of infringing AI output from AI training data. It also allows fair use for copyright protected AI training data only where the works were legally obtained which still gives room for compensation to copyright owners which ensures that copyright does not stifle technological advancement.

title: Analysis of ASCON Lightweight Authenticated Encryption for UAV Surveillance Communication Security
abstract: The advancement of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology has brought attention to the necessity of secure communication in intelligence and surveillance missions. UAV systems are susceptible to a number of cybersecurity threats since they depend on wireless communication, including eavesdropping, spoofing, replay attacks, telemetry manipulation, and hijacking. Although traditional cryptography techniques offer robust security, their high computational and energy costs render them unsuitable for the limited capabilities of UAVs. This study employs a comparative literature assessment of papers published between 2021 and 2026 to analyse ASCON lightweight cryptography as a potential solution for secure UAV surveillance communications. Confidentiality, integrity verification, authentication capabilities, and overall computational and energy efficiency against significant threats are important factors evaluated. The results demonstrate how effectively ASCON supports Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD), which provides total security for confidentiality, integrity, and authentication while consuming little energy and computing resources. Additionally, ASCON is more resilient to spoofing and replay attacks than other conventional and lightweight cryptographic methods. This study highlights ASCON's capabilities in limited operating conditions and promotes the use of lightweight authenticated encryption algorithms in future UAV cybersecurity frameworks and embedded surveillance systems.

This study employs a comparative literature assessment of papers published between 2021 and 2026 to analyse ASCON lightweight cryptography as a potential solution for secure UAV surveillance communications. Confidentiality, integrity verification, authentication capabilities, and overall computational and energy efficiency against significant threats are important factors evaluated. The results demonstrate how effectively ASCON supports Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD), which provides total security for confidentiality, integrity, and authentication while consuming little energy and computing resources. Additionally, ASCON is more resilient to spoofing and replay attacks than other conventional and lightweight cryptographic methods. This study highlights ASCON's capabilities in limited operating conditions and promotes the use of lightweight authenticated encryption algorithms in future UAV cybersecurity frameworks and embedded surveillance systems.

title: Real-Time Internet of Things Predictive Analytics for On-Grid Solar Power and Efficiency in Tropical Smart Cities
abstract: The performance of On-Grid Solar Power Plants is strongly influenced by environmental conditions, particularly solar irradiance and module temperature. Therefore, an accurate prediction model is required to evaluate system performance under actual operating conditions. Previous studies have generally relied on historical meteorological datasets or simulation-based approaches and have rarely integrated real-time Internet of Things (IoT) monitoring with PVsyst simulation, Simulink modeling, and Multiple Linear Regression (MLR) within a unified predictive framework. This study aims to develop a predictive model for the output power and efficiency of a 160.05 kWp On-Grid Solar Power Plant installed at the Integrated Waste Processing Facility, Sepaku District, North Penajam Paser Regency, East Kalimantan. The novelty of this research lies in the integration of real-time IoT monitoring, PVsyst simulation, Simulink modeling, and MLR to estimate photovoltaic output power and system efficiency under actual operating conditions. The proposed model integrates real-time IoT-based monitoring, PVsyst simulation, Simulink modeling, and MLR. Real-time operational data, including solar irradiance and module temperature, were used to develop and validate the prediction model. The PVsyst simulation estimated an annual energy production of 58,418.25 kWh with a Performance Ratio (PR) of 78.30%. Model validation produced a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 3.15% for output power prediction and 2.38% for system efficiency prediction, indicating high prediction accuracy. The developed model can accurately predict the output power and efficiency of the On-Grid Solar Power Plant and can be used to support performance evaluation based on actual operational data.

title: A STUDY ON ROLE OF AI IN SHAPING E – COMMERCE
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming very important in online shopping. As more people shop online, companies use AI to understand what customers like and make shopping easier. AI tools like recommendations, chatbots, and data analysis help suggest products, answer questions quickly, and give each shopper a more personal and convenient experience.AI also helps e-commerce businesses manage their daily operations more efficiently. It supports tasks such as predicting customer demand, managing inventory, optimizing supply chains, adjusting prices, and detecting fraud. By using AI to analyze large amounts of data, companies can make smarter decisions, save time, and reduce costs. This allows businesses to operate more smoothly and respond faster to changing market conditions.Using AI in online shopping also has some challenges. Companies need to be careful about privacy, security, ethical use of customer data, and high costs. Overall, AI helps e-commerce grow, making shopping faster, easier, and more customer-friendly, and will be very important for the future of online stores.

title: The Carlo Cognitive Engine: A Minimal State Machine for Belief, Contradiction, and Collapse — Formally Specified, Formally Proved
abstract: The Carlo Cognitive Engine is a small, fully deterministic state machine for modeling how a bounded set of beliefs is admitted, contested, and resolved. It has no learning, no probability, and no randomness anywhere in its definition — by design. What it offers instead is a guarantee that is easy to state and, in this release, formally proved: the same sequence of inputs always produces the same output state, with every intermediate step recorded in an append-only log. It is offered here as a compact, fully specified, fully reference-implemented and reproducibility-tested artifact: a small enough system to read end to end in one sitting, yet structurally rich enough to sit at the intersection of half a dozen established research traditions. What's in this release A complete, ten-section deterministic specification covering the engine's eight cognitive primitives, its nine-state machine, its four reasoning pathways, its contradiction-resolution rule, its reset operator, its execution model, its formal mathematical backbone, its I/O contract, and its safety guarantees. An interactive, single-file HTML reference implementation: a live, animated, neural-network-style diagram of the engine's seven architectural layers, with a working control panel (frame, assert, trigger contradiction, reset, full auto-run, JSON export) so the formal claims below can be watched happening, not just read. A researcher manual with worked examples, a complete contradiction-resolution truth table, a formal grammar for the input language, complexity notes, a glossary, and the cross-domain context summarized below. An extended mathematical appendix with formal definitions and proofs (not just assertions) of determinism, reproducibility, collapse commutativity and idempotence, tie-break uniqueness, and an inductive proof that the engine's capacity bound can never be violated. The mathematics, briefly The engine's full behavior is captured by a state vector S = (phase, frame, assertions, resetCount, cycle) and a single total, deterministic transition function T : S × I → S, where I is the impulse alphabet generated by a small regular grammar (frame, assert, reset). Contradictions are resolved by a collapse function C(a,b) that selects the higher-priority assertion under a fixed total order (EXPLICIT > DERIVED > INHERITED > DEFAULT), with ties broken by insertion order — a rule proved in the appendix to be total, commutative (C(a,b) = C(b,a)), and idempotent (C(a,a) = a). A reset function R(S) returns the engine to a canonical ready state. The headline result, the Reproducibility Axiom, states that replaying any finite impulse sequence from the same starting state always yields the same resulting state — and because T is defined by total case analysis with no underspecified branch and no external source of randomness, this is proved directly rather than merely asserted. A companion proof shows, by induction on sequence length, that the engine's assertion-capacity bound can never be exceeded: the implementation forces a collapse before admission whenever capacity is reached, so the bound holds by construction, not by convention. Where this sits across research domains None of the following are claims of equivalence — they are orientation points for anyone trying to place this design relative to existing literature: Automata theory — the engine is, structurally, a Mealy machine (finite states, a regular input alphabet, a total transition and output function); its grammar is provably regular. Knowledge representation & belief revision — the frame/assertion/contradiction/collapse cycle echoes justification-based truth maintenance systems (Doyle, de Kleer) and AGM-style belief revision, with the fixed priority order playing a role similar to an epistemic entrenchment ordering. Non-monotonic logic — admitting new information can force retraction of previously held assertions, a defining feature of non-monotonic reasoning systems. Paraconsistent logic, by contrast — where paraconsistent systems tolerate contradiction without collapse, this engine does the opposite by design: contradictions are never tolerated and are always resolved within one tick. Distributed systems — the Reproducibility Axiom is exactly the determinism property underlying state-machine replication in consensus protocols: the same operation log, replayed anywhere, must produce the same state. Cognitive architectures — the frame/assert/contradict/collapse/stabilize/emit cycle loosely parallels the match-select-fire cycle of production-system architectures such as ACT-R or Soar, with the contradiction state echoing Soar's notion of an impasse. Control theory — the state vector and total transition function frame the system as a discrete-time, deterministic dynamical system with stability guaranteed by construction rather than derived asymptotically. Category theory — currying the transition function yields a monoid homomorphism from impulse sequences (under concatenation) to state-space endofunctions (under composition); the Reproducibility Axiom is precisely the well-definedness of that homomorphism. Computability theory — every function in the engine's core is total and computable over finite domains: no partiality, no divergence, no unbounded search. Suggested use As a minimal, auditable teaching example for deterministic state machines and truth-maintenance concepts; as a small reference artifact for discussions of reproducibility and replay-determinism; or as a starting point for extensions — nested frames, graded belief, multi-agent variants, or a concurrent transition model — each of which the accompanying manual identifies as open, unspecified territory rather than papering over. Designed, specified, and reference-implemented by Matthew Arthur Carlo. title: SkewQSC_Repo: Reproducibility package for Synchronization Recovery via Ore Polynomial Orbits
abstract: This archive contains the reproducibility package for the manuscript "Synchronization Recovery via Ore Polynomial Orbits: A Skew-Cyclic Algebraic Framework for Quantum Codes." The package includes finite-field arithmetic, Ore-polynomial arithmetic, monic right-divisor enumeration, skew-cycliccode construction routines, minimum-distance verification, bounded-distance q-ary syndrome decoding, and Monte Carloperformance-evaluation scripts. The main verification script is verify.py, which regenerates the computational checks reported in the manuscript,including the length-8 marker construction, the skew-index divisibility checks, the matched-gain landscape, positive-rate CSS constructions, and exhaustive weight-1 bit/phase decoder checks. The performance script is performance.py, which reports Monte Carlo bit-decoder, phase-decoder, and combined successestimates for the flagship positive-rate skew-cyclic CSS codes. The code uses only the Python standard library.

title: Fine-tuning XTREME-R tasks for low-resource zero-shot transfer
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does fine-tuning on non-English intermediate tasks from XTREME-R affect zero-shot transfer accuracy to low-resource languages compared to English-only fine-tuning? title: AutoScale-ML with HASA: A Docker-Based Framework for Distributed AutoML Model Selection
abstract: This paper presents AutoScale-ML with HASA, a hierarchical adaptive search framework for automated machine learning (AutoML) model selection, implemented within a simulated seven-node distributed computing environment consisting of one master node and six independent Docker containers, each exposing a REST endpoint through Flask.Each worker trains a randomly assigned Scikit-learn classifier drawn from RandomForest, GradientBoosting, ExtraTrees, DecisionTree, and LogisticRegression on a 50,000-sample synthetic classification dataset (50 features, 20 informative) generated via scikit-learn's make_classification, and returns accuracy, training runtime, simulated network delay, and a composite score to a central master process.The master applies a three-phase Hierarchical Adaptive Search Algorithm (HASA): Phase 1 collects all six worker evaluations and retains the top-4 by composite score; Phase 2 re-ranks those four candidates and retains the top-2; Phase 3 selects the single best model by maximum composite score.Experimental results-including per-model benchmarks, phase-by-phase HASA traces, penalty coefficient sensitivity analysis, and network delay characterisation-demonstrate that the framework effectively balances prediction accuracy and computational efficiency through runtime-aware hierarchical model selection.Comprehensive evaluation across five classifier families reveals that the composite scoring function heavily penalises ensemble training times, often favouring lightweight models over higheraccuracy alternatives.The penalty coefficient α is shown to be a critical first-class configuration parameter that must be calibrated to deployment context.The findings highlight the framework's usefulness as a reproducible baseline for containerised AutoML experimentation.

title: Analisis Sentimen Terhadap Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) pada Media Sosial Menggunakan Algoritma IndoBERT
abstract: The Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Program is one of the Indonesian government's strategic policies that has generated various public responses on social media, particularly TikTok. This study aims to analyze public sentiment toward the MBG program using the IndoBERT Deep Learning model. The data were collected through TikTok comment scraping using the Apify platform, resulting in 14,447 raw comments. After the data cleaning process, 13,574 valid comments were obtained, and a 50% sample was selected, resulting in 6,787 comments for modeling purposes. Sentiment labeling was performed automatically using a lexicon-based approach with three sentiment categories: positive, negative, and neutral. The class imbalance problem was addressed using the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) on the training data prior to the IndoBERT fine-tuning process. The results showed that the IndoBERT model with SMOTE achieved an accuracy of 72.39% and a weighted F1-score of 0.73. Although SMOTE improved the representation of the minority class, it reduced the overall accuracy when compared to the model without SMOTE. Nevertheless, the model was still able to classify public sentiment toward the MBG program reasonably well. The findings of this study are expected to provide useful insights for the government in understanding public perceptions of the MBG policy through social media.

abstract: The rapid expansion of smart ecosystems driven by Internet of Things (IoT) technologies requires real-time data processing that is secure, efficient, and capable of handling large-scale heterogeneous data streams.Traditional centralized learning approaches often struggle with latency, bandwidth constraints, and privacy risks due to the continuous transfer of raw data.This study aims to optimize smart ecosystem performance by integrating Federated Learning (FL) as a distributed intelligence framework for real-time IoT data processing.The proposed model allows multiple IoT nodes to collaboratively train a global model without sharing raw data, thereby enhancing privacy protection and reducing network load.Experimental results demonstrate that FL provides higher accuracy, better scalability, and improved resilience compared to centralized systems, especially in environments with diverse sensor distributions.These findings confirm that Federated Learning is a highly promising approach for strengthening smart ecosystem reliability, responsiveness, and data security.This research contributes to developing future-ready IoT architectures capable of supporting intelligent, decentralized, and privacy-preserving environments

title: Optimalisasi Algoritma Fuzzy Gustafson-Kessel dengan Variasi Parameter Weighting Exponent untuk Clustering Data Risiko Depresi Pelajar
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh variasi nilai weighting exponent pada algoritma Fuzzy Gustafson-Kessel dalam proses clustering data risiko depresi pelajar. Data yang digunakan berjumlah 502 responden dengan tujuh variabel yang merepresentasikan faktor akademik, finansial, dan gaya hidup. Tahapan penelitian meliputi preprocessing data menggunakan label encoding dan normalisasi, dilanjutkan dengan proses clustering pada beberapa variasi nilai weighting exponent. Kualitas hasil clustering dievaluasi menggunakan Xie-Beni Index sebagai ukuran kekompakan dan keterpisahan cluster. title: Development and Pilot Testing of the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality in Sport Scale (EAIVRS)
abstract: This repository contains the official version of the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality in Sport Scale (EAIVRS), including the original English instrument, the Portuguese version used during the pilot study, the methodological protocol, supplementary materials and documentation supporting the development of the scale. The EAIVRS was developed to assess professionals' ethical perceptions regarding the implementation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Virtual Reality (VR) in Physical Education and Sport. The instrument comprises four dimensions: Ethical Concerns, Educational Value, Trust and Future Intention. title: Human-Centered Explainable AI in Education
abstract: This chapter explores the integration of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in educational contexts through a human-centered lens, examining how AI-driven insights can be meaningfully aligned with the diverse needs of students and educators. As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power educational technologies, their ability to provide natural language explanations presents unprecedented opportunities for personalized learning support and intuitive AI interaction. However, deploying LLM-based XAI systems in educational environments introduces complex challenges requiring careful consideration. The chapter examines the paradoxical nature of using LLMs for explainability — while these models can generate seemingly coherent explanations, their internal mechanisms remain fundamentally opaque. Drawing from human-centered design principles, this work proposes a comprehensive approach for trusted LLM implementation in educational contexts, incorporating safety guardrails, retrieval augmented generation, advanced reasoning techniques, and virtual persona testing methodologies. The approach emphasizes continuous human oversight and stake holder involvement as essential components for responsible deployment. The chapter concludes by outlining validation strategies and future directions for ethical XAI implementation in educational settings.

title: From Local Explanations to Collective Explanations
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in education raises major issues of transparency and explainability, which are essential to build trust and guide pedagogical decisions. Local explanation methods, such as LIME, provide useful but limited insights, as they remain unstable, focused on isolated cases, and poorly suited for identifying collective trends. To overcome these limitations, we propose an innovative approach that combines three complementary dimensions: local explanations (LIME), inter-model aggregation, and clustering of explanatory contributions. Few studies in the literature simultaneously integrate these three axes to generate collective educational profiles, which gives our approach an original contribution in this research field. This methodology transforms complex individual explanations into robust collective profiles, offering a deep understanding of learning dynamics. The results reveal differentiated profiles—ranging from fundamental sciences to computer science and prior academic background—reflecting the plurality of learning and performance dynamics. These profiles constitute concrete action levers for teachers and institutions, promoting personalization, equity, and accountability in the use of educational technologies. By linking local interpretability to collective explanation, this chapter proposes a robust framework aligning AI contributions with human-centered pedagogical objectives.

title: A Shallow Embedding of Datalog in Lean
abstract: Datalog is a lightweight logic programming language, based on the logic of Horn clauses. Lean, on the other hand, is a proof assistant system and language based on the Calculus of Inductive Constructions (CIC). Datalog is more constrained and less expressive than Lean but has a long history of established deduction algorithms. Writing definitions and queries in the Datalog fragment of Lean would be more succinct and understandable than writing them in Lean itself.

title: At the Precipice of Integrity Protection using Pointer Authentication
abstract: Despite more than a decade of availability in CPUs, the adoption of fine-grained hardware-assisted memory safety in commercial platforms and computing systems has been slow and is today mainly available in closed mobile ecosystems. Likely reasons for this are unpractical requirements on development and the emergence of compatibility issues between code that leverages the security hardware assistance, and code that does not.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Spacecraft Attitude Control During Atmospheric Re-Entry
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has the potential to solve attitude control problems more adaptively, precisely, and robustly by handling nonlinear dynamics, uncertainties, and failure cases more effectively than traditional attitude control approaches. We explore reinforcement learning (RL) for attitude control in spacecraft re-entry. An industry-standard proportional-integral-derivative controller with gain scheduling serves as a strong baseline for model-free RL and hybrid controllers that combine these two approaches. We formalize the application in the RL framework to apply continuous, off-policy RL. State-of-the-art RL achieves comparable performance to traditional control approaches in this domain. However, its out-of-distribution generalization is not sufficient. Hence, we use dynamics randomization to introduce challenging task variations during training and enforce generalization in a predefined operational envelope. Finally, we assess the best obtained RL-based controllers with application-specific metrics to show superior performance in comparison to traditional controllers in the operational envelope, that is, hybrid controllers are able to track the angle of attack better and are more robust under variations of mass, inertia tensor, and flap actuator bandwidth.

title: Decoding Audience Sentiments on the ‘Mann ki Baat’ Radio Broadcast Using Data Mining Approaches
abstract: The popularity of any government depends on the ability to communicate with the common people and that effectively conveys its policies, initiatives, and future goals.Political leaders around the nation employ a variety of communication techniques to engage with the public and inform them of their endeavours. Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi chooses radio podcasts as a medium to reach out to the common people through the programme ‘Mann ki Baat’ since it is a significant communication medium that transmits podcasts to remote areas - villages, districts, and cities. In order to connect with as many people as possible, the “Mann ki Baat” programme is also broadcasted on several social media sites, including YouTube. And, the present study deals with the contents of the videos of Mann ki Baat uploaded on the YouTube channel National Doordarshan and the analysis of the comments posted by the listeners. The analysis of all the comments revealed that Mann ki Baat is a direct radio programme thatfosters a link between the people and the PM himself. A larger number of comments are heavily concentrated on PM Modi rather than the content of the programme. Numerous residents make use of this channel to express their joy, rage, and enthusiasm. This research offers recommendations to investigate the critical comments of ordinary men to improve the environment in which they dwell.

title: An Intelligent Adaptive Learning Framework for Uzbek Language Teaching Using Dynamic Parameter Adaptation
abstract: The emergence of intelligent and personalized digital education and the shortcomings of the conventional language teaching system including conventional learning resources and conventional teaching techniques are apparent. The necessity of personalized and intelligent digital education has exposed the shortcomings of conventional language teaching systems that mainly use static learning resources and teaching techniques that do not take into consideration any difference between students. In order to solve these shortcomings, in this paper, the Intelligent Adaptive Learning Framework for Uzbek Language Teaching Using Dynamic Parameter Adaptation (IALF-DPA) is proposed. The uniqueness of the proposed framework is that it incorporates continuous learner profiling, attention-based deep learning to predict learner's performance, adaptive content recommendation and dynamic parameter adaptation (DPA) technique which continuously adapts the level of difficulty of the lesson, order of content delivery and revision schedule according to learner's performance in real time. Unlike existing adaptive learning frameworks which are based on predefined adaptation rules, it constantly adapts the instructional parameters according to the learner's accuracy, reaction time, error pattern and knowledge acquisition. The proposed framework was evaluated using the benchmark data set of Uzbek language learning which had vocabulary, grammar, reading, and writing tests conducted among learners of different skill levels. The experimental evaluation of the proposed IALF-DPA system indicates that the suggested system has achieved higher accuracy (97.84%), higher precision (97.32%), higher recall (97.11%), higher F1-score (97.21%), higher learner completion rate (95.68%), and higher knowledge retention rate (95.13%) as compared to the existing approaches of adaptive learning. Thus, the above results validate that the use of DPA helps to increase the engagement and effectiveness of learning in intelligent Uzbek language teaching and learning.

title: AN INVESTIGATION INTO CLASS IMBALANCE PROBLEM IN ANALYZING THE UTILITY OF USER REVIEWS IN DIGITAL DISTRIBUTION SYSTEMS
abstract: This paper examines the problem of class imbalance in building machine learning models for automatically classifying the helpfulness of user reviews on the Steam platform. An analysis of over 6 million reviews revealed that the proportion of helpful reviews is approximately 15%, leading to an "accuracy paradox" when training standard classifiers. A comparative study of sample balancing methods-class weighting and majority class undersampling-is conducted.

title: Implementasi Metode Certainty Factor untuk Diagnosa Dini Tuberkulosis (TBC) Paru dan Ekstra Paru Berbasis Web
abstract: Tuberkulosis (TBC) merupakan penyakit menular akibat bakteri Mycobacterium tuberculosis yang masih menimbulkan beban kesehatan tinggi. Gejala TBC sering tumpang tindih dengan penyakit lain, sehingga tenaga kesehatan maupun masyarakat kerap menemui kendala saat melakukan identifikasi awal, terutama ketika akses ke fasilitas dan tenaga ahli terbatas. Penelitian ini mengembangkan sistem pakar berbasis web untuk membantu diagnosis dini TBC paru dan ekstra paru menggunakan metode Certainty Factor (CF) agar sistem dapat memodelkan ketidakpastian hubungan gejala dan penyakit. Penelitian menyusun basis pengetahuan dari studi literatur dan wawancara tenaga kesehatan, lalu memetakan pengetahuan ke dalam aturan (rule) serta bobot keyakinan yang direpresentasikan melalui nilai measure of belief dan measure of disbelief. Peneliti merancang aplikasi secara terstruktur melalui tahapan akuisisi pengetahuan, perancangan proses dan aliran data (flowchart, context diagram, dan data flow diagram), perancangan basis data, implementasi modul konsultasi, kemudian pengujian. Pengujian mencakup uji fungsional (blackbox) untuk memastikan setiap fitur berjalan sesuai kebutuhan, serta uji akurasi dengan membandingkan hasil perhitungan CF sistem terhadap diagnosis tenaga medis pada data uji. Sistem mengolah input gejala dari pengguna, menghitung tingkat kepastian setiap hipotesis penyakit, dan menampilkan diagnosis dengan nilai keyakinan serta rekomendasi penanganan. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan sistem memberikan hasil diagnosis dengan tingkat akurasi sebesar 85% dibandingkan diagnosis pakar, sehingga sistem dapat berperan sebagai alat bantu skrining awal TBC secara lebih cepat dan sistematis.

title: A Study on the Development and Applicability of the G-MADE HIVE Collaborative Landscape Preliminary Review Support Model Based on Generative AI Personas and Human Experts
abstract: This study developed and examined the applicability of the G-MADE HIVE collaborative landscape pre-review support model based on generative AI personas and human experts. A research framework integrating expert groups, citizen groups, verification panels, and a Multi-AI Expert Cluster was established based on landscape pre-review and AIHuman Hybrid theories. The results showed that human experts excelled in public value and contextual interpretation, whereas generative AI demonstrated strengths in criteria-based review, structured analysis, and explainability. To address these complementary characteristics, the study proposed the G-MADE HIVE Evaluation System using domain-specific AI personas and a Multi-AI Expert Cluster based on ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. The proposed model integrates expert groups, citizen groups, and verification panels into a multilayer Hybrid review system.

title: UNLOCKING SANSKRIT WITH AI – OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES
abstract: Combining Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Sanskrit opens up exciting new ways to study one of the world’s oldest languages. This paper looks at the big opportunities and the difficult challenges of using modern technology to revive and understand Sanskrit.Sanskrit is a very logical language with strict grammar rules. This makes it a perfect match for AI and computer programming. Today, AI gives us the opportunity to scan and digitize thousands of ancient handwritten scrolls using smart tools. It also helps create apps that act like personal teachers, making it easier for anyone to learn the language. Automated translation is another big plus, helping to share ancient Indian wisdom about science and philosophy with the whole world in many different languages.However, there are still challenges to overcome. One major problem is that we don’t have enough typed-out data to train AI models properly. Also, Sanskrit is complex because words often blend together, which can confuse standard computers. We must also be careful to respect the cultural and religious importance of these texts. In conclusion, while AI can lead to a “Sanskrit rebirth,” it works best when computer experts and traditional scholars work together to preserve this heritage for future generations.

title: QUANTUM TRANSFORMER NETWORKS FOR REAL-TIME ANOMALY DETECTION AND PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS IN INDUSTRIAL IOT ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) technologies have fast grown into a field for intelligent automation, real-time monitoring, and data-driven decision-making in today's industrial environments. Increased connectivity of industrial devices has also brought with it many challenges regarding anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and cyber security. Efficiently managing high-dimensional data, learning long-range dependence and complex patterns of abnormality from dynamic industrial systems is often difficult using traditional machine learning and deep learning methods. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper introduces a Quantum Transformer Network (QTN) for real-time data analysis and anomaly detection in real-world scenarios of Industrial IoT. The proposed system combines the feature optimization capabilities of quantum computing with the contextual learning approach of Transformer to enhance anomaly detection and subsequent event forecasting. First, the data collected by Industrial IoT is preprocessed and normalized, and then, redundant and irrelevant data attributes are extracted by analyzing feature dependency with the help of quantum technology. An adaptive predictive analytics module is integrated to anticipate possible failures and abnormal operating actions before they happen. Experimental results on Industrial IoT datasets show the superiority of the proposed QTN model over the current models, such as TranAD, Graph Transformer, and Health-BERT models. It achieves 95.3% accuracy, 94.5% precision, 94.4% recall, 94.4% F1-score, 95.9% specificity, 96.5% AUC, with low detection latency and computational cost. The results obtained show that the proposed Quantum Transformer Network can serve as an effective, scalable, and intelligent solution for anomaly detection and predictive analytics in the next-generation Industrial IoT systems.

The results obtained show that the proposed Quantum Transformer Network can serve as an effective, scalable, and intelligent solution for anomaly detection and predictive analytics in the next-generation Industrial IoT systems.

title: SynGuide: Artifact for Enhancing Grammar-Constrained Neural Proof Synthesis with Neuro-Symbolic Guidance
abstract: This artifact contains the source code, scripts, model configurations, and normalized evaluation outputs for SynGuide, a neuro-symbolic decoding framework for enhancing syntax-constrained neural proof synthesis in Rocq. SynGuide introduces structured proof guidance at different stages of grammar-constrained tactic generation, including proof-intent-guided tactic prediction, retrieved-lemma grounding, and diversity-aware candidate selection. The artifact provides integrations with multiple neural theorem prover backends, including ASTactic, Passport, and the Tac and Tok configurations derived from TacTok. It also contains training and evaluation entry points, CoqGym-related utilities, project-level lemma resources, grammar definitions, and per-file JSON evaluation outputs. The Result_files/ directory contains normalized results for the complete SynGuide configuration and the following ablation settings: init: the original syntax-constrained prover configuration; w/o proof-intent/function guidance: SynGuide without the proof-intent functional layer; w/o retrieved lemma grounding: SynGuide without project-level retrieved lemmas during argument generation; w/o diversity-aware candidate selection: SynGuide without structural diversity guidance during beam selection. The proof-intent layer organizes tactics according to the functional taxonomy explicitly encoded in tactics.ebnf. The taxonomy contains the following six categories: Functional category Primary purpose Tactics defined in tactics.ebnf Proof framework construction Constructs the basic proof structure by introducing premises, decomposing top-level logical connectives, selecting constructors, or directly supplying evidence. intro, intros, split, left, right, exists, constructor, exact, assumption Goal decomposition and transformation Decomposes inductive structures or transforms goals into forms that are easier to prove through case analysis, induction, unfolding, and reduction. destruct, induction, generalize, simple induction, case, elim, unfold, simpl, cbn, cbv, red, hnf, idtac Equality reasoning Solves, rewrites, reverses, decomposes, or derives information from equality relations. reflexivity, rewrite, symmetry, f_equal, subst, injection Logical reasoning and contradiction Applies known propositions, analyzes hypotheses, derives contradictions, and changes the current proof obligation through logical reasoning. apply, inversion, inversion_clear, contradiction, contradict, discriminate, exfalso, trivial Automated reasoning Delegates proof search or domain-specific reasoning to general-purpose or specialized automation procedures. auto, eauto, tauto, intuition, congruence, easy, ring, field, lia, omega Proof-context management Modifies, reorganizes, or specializes hypotheses in the local proof context. clear, revert, specialize This classification is used as a symbolic functional layer above the original tactic grammar. Rather than making a hard proof-intent decision, SynGuide scores complete grammar paths from functional categories to concrete tactics, allowing tactics from all valid categories to remain available during decoding. The artifact is intended to support reproduction of the training, proof-search, ablation, and cross-prover evaluation workflows reported in the accompanying paper. External dependencies—including the CoqGym dataset, Rocq/Coq, SerAPI, CoqHammer, OPAM packages, and the Python environment—must be prepared according to the accompanying README.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Based Cyberbullying Classification System
abstract: The increasing use of social media and digital communication tools has brought many advantages, yet it has also enabled the concerning issue of cyberbullying which involves the use of digital platforms to harass, threaten, dishonour or demean individuals.Techniques to reduce this problem to a certain extent have already been introduced in online systems.However, they possess limitations of usage and lack of explainability.This research presents the development and evaluation of an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) based cyberbullying classification system intended to detect and interpret harmful content on social media platforms.The system leverages textual and symbolic features from usergenerated contents, extracted from social media platform, X (Twitter), to classify posts as bullying or non-bullying.The methodology adopted in this work include data preprocessing (tokenization, stemming, lemmatization, and TF-IDF vectorization), followed by model training using Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Multinomial Naive Bayes (MNB) classifiers.To address the class imbalance in the dataset, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) was employed, which resulted in improved model fairness and performance.Among the models that were tested, Logistic Regression achieved the highest generalization accuracy of 93.12%.In other to enhance transparency and trust, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was integrated, which offered interpretable insights into model predictions and highlights key linguistic features influencing classification results.The system was deployed via a web interface which enables real-time content moderation.While the results demonstrate high accuracy and interpretability, the study also reflects ethical considerations such as contextual misclassification, societal bias, and data privacy.

title: Penerapan Algoritma Logistic Regression dalam Deteksi Komentar Promosi Judi Online pada YouTube
abstract: The growing popularity of video-based social media platforms such as YouTube has significantly increased user interaction through comment sections. However, this high level of activity has also led to the misuse of comment sections to promote online gambling through various writing patterns intended to disguise specific keywords. This study aims to detect online gambling promotional comments on YouTube using a text mining approach. The framework applied in this study consists of several stages, including text preprocessing, keyword-based feature engineering, TF-IDF feature extraction using character n-grams, data balancing through the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), and classification using the Logistic Regression algorithm. The dataset used in this study consists of 11,972 YouTube comments obtained from a YouTube video comment section and manually labeled into two classes: normal comments and online gambling promotional comments. The evaluation results show that the model achieved a precision of 1.000, recall of 0.912, F1-score of 0.954, and overall accuracy of 0.999 on the test data. These findings indicate that the combination of keyword-based features, character n-gram TF-IDF, SMOTE, and Logistic Regression can effectively detect online gambling promotional comments, particularly in minimizing the misclassification of normal comments as promotional gambling content.

title: Оцінка ефективності впровадження інтелектуальних помічників у системи електронної комерції: методологія та практичні результати
abstract: У статті розглянуто актуальну проблему інтеграції систем штучного інтелекту (ШІ), зокрема інтелектуальних помічників, у сферу електронної комерції. Проаналізовано обмеження традиційних методів підтримки клієнтів та обґрунтовано необхідність переходу до автоматизованих рішень. Основною метою роботи є розробка комплексної методики кількісної оцінки ефективності ШІ-асистентів. Запропоновано математичну модель, що базується на синтезі фінансових (Return on Investment, економія витрат), поведінкових (Customer Lifetime Value, конверсія) та технічних метрик. Вперше введено поняття “коефіцієнта довіри” користувача для корекції показників ефективної конверсії. На основі розробленої методології проведено порівняльний аналіз результатів впровадження ШІ у провідних технологічних компаніях. Результати експериментального дослідження підтверджують пряму кореляцію між використанням інтелектуальних помічників та зростанням ключових бізнес-показників, зокрема скороченням операційних витрат до 50 % та зростанням конверсії. Практична цінність роботи полягає у створенні універсального інструментарію для оцінки доцільності інвестицій у технології штучного інтелекту.

title: A Generative AI-Enabled Contextual Data Curation Framework for Emerging Demographic Health and Malaria Indicator Survey Data
abstract: The increasing complexity and volume of demographic health and malaria indicators surveys data from diverse sources present significant challenges for effective data curation and contextual interpretation pipeline, especially in machine learning applications reliant on curated data to improve its predictive performance. While Generative AI has advanced language understanding, its integration into data curation frameworks remains underexplored. This paper proposes an intelligent framework that embeds Generative AI algorithms into NLP model to enhance semantic representation of data during real-time curation, focusing on analysis that transforms textual contents to equivalent fact embeddings representations required for machine learning. By embedding Generative AI algorithms over conventional data preprocessing approach, the framework improves both the efficiency and accuracy of contextual data interpretation, enabling more robust machine learning task for evidence-based decision-making. Experimental results with selected tree-based algorithms demonstrate that our approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of average accuracy (F1-Score) of approximately 5%, with data obtained from Nigeria demographic health and Malaria indicator surveys. This signifies the imperative contextually representing curated data for machine learning task, as it enhances the quality of outputs and supports evidence-based decision-making.
